original_draft: This matter arises from a breach of a written Supply Agreement between Meridian Logistics, Inc. and Northgate Packaging Solutions, LLC [E1]. On January 15, 2021, the parties agreed that Northgate would deliver 50,000 corrugated shipping containers per month at a fixed price of $2.40 per unit [E1]. The dispute began in March 2021 when Northgate delivered only 32,000 units, falling 18,000 units short of the contractual minimum [E2]. On April 2, 2021, Meridian sent a written notice of breach demanding cure within thirty days [E2]. Northgate failed to cure, and in May 2021 deliveries fell further to 21,000 units before Northgate suspended all shipments on June 10, 2021, citing a raw-material shortage [E3]. As a direct result, Meridian procured replacement containers on the open market at $3.85 per unit, incurring approximately $1.2 million in cover damages [E4]. Meridian seeks compensatory damages of not less than $1,200,000, pre-judgment interest, and costs of suit [E4].
edited_draft:
Breach of a written Supply Agreement between Plaintiff and Defendant [E1].

Timeline:
- Jan 15, 2021: Parties sign Supply Agreement; Defendant to deliver 50,000 containers/month at $2.40/unit [E1].
- Mar 2021: Defendant delivers only 32,000 units, 18,000 short of the minimum [E2].
- Apr 2, 2021: Plaintiff serves written notice of breach, 30-day cure demand [E2].
- May 2021: Deliveries fall to 21,000 units; no cure [E3].
- Jun 10, 2021: Defendant suspends all shipments, citing raw-material shortage [E3].

Damages: Plaintiff covered at $3.85/unit, incurring ~$1.2M [E4]. Relief sought: $1,200,000 plus pre-judgment interest and costs [E4].
